study_identification.title: Rightward brain structural asymmetry in young children with autism

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate atypical development of gray matter volume (GMV) asymmetry in young children with ASD (with and without DD/ID) and DD/ID only, and its association with behavioral/clinical measures and gene transcription profiles.

quality_checking_detail.answer: Raw structural images were independently manually inspected by two staff members to exclude those with obvious motion artefacts. After quality control, the preprocessing steps included skull stripping, and realignment using CAT12 and then reregistered and segmented based on the Chinese pediatric atlases (CHN-PD). Then, we conducted the second round of quality control, comprising algorithms and a manual inspection of the segmentation results.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: The ComBat analysis based on an empirical Bayes approach was utilized to harmonize the site effects.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study used ComBat for site effect harmonization, which is a method to handle nuisance structure. However, the paper does not provide a detailed evaluation of how well this handled the nuisance structure.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: The ComBat analysis based on an empirical Bayes approach was utilized to harmonize the site effects [43-45].

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study used 5-fold cross-validation to test the robustness of the normative model.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: Fivefold cross-validation was conducted to avoid over /uniFB01 tting and obtain optimal parameters. and The regional similarities across subjects between original GMV asymmetry deviations and each validation fold were shown in Fig. S3.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not mention using an independent dataset from the same domain for validation.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study does not mention using a dataset from a different domain for validation.

diseases_studied.answer: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD); Developmental delay/intellectual disability (DD/ID)

clinical_groups_n.answer: ASD with DD/ID: 563; ASD without DD/ID: 212; DD/ID only: 36

clinical_groups_age.answer: ASD with DD/ID: 3.98 ± 1.22 years; ASD without DD/ID: 3.24 ± 1.15 years; DD/ID only: 4.42 ± 1.4 years

clinical_groups_sex.answer: ASD with DD/ID: M 472 (83.8%); ASD without DD/ID: M 184 (86.8%); DD/ID only: M 25 (69.4%)

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) to explore the associations between brain structural asymmetry deviations and behavioural scores. Partial least squares (PLS) regression analysis and between-region similarity analysis to explore associations with transcriptional profiles.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study found a common rightward GMV asymmetry in young ASD children, which is related to ASD symptoms and specific gene expression profiles.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study identified a common abnormal pattern of GMV asymmetry across all ASD children: more rightward laterality in the inferior parietal lobe and precentral gyrus, and higher individual variability in the temporal pole. ASD with DD/ID children showed a severer and more extensive abnormal pattern in GMV asymmetry deviation values, which was linked with both ASD symptoms and verbal IQ. The abnormal pattern of ASD without DD/ID children showed higher and more extensive individual variability, which was linked with ASD symptoms only. DD/ID children showed no significant differences from healthy population in asymmetry. The GMV laterality patterns of all patient groups were significantly associated with both shared and unique gene expression profiles.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: 1. VBM methodology confounders. 2. Limited environmental factors in the normative model. 3. Linking child brain data to adult gene expression data. 4. Unbalanced sex ratio.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The findings reveal the potency of brain asymmetry as a mediator variable for multiscale cascade analysis in developmental disorders and provides insights to the potential neural mechanisms.

general_notes.general_notes: The study used a large sample of young children, which is a strength. The use of normative modeling allowed for the investigation of individual-level deviations. The multiscale approach, linking brain structure to clinical symptoms and gene expression, is a novel aspect of this study.
